title: Mexico Delivers 58 Tonnes of Earthquake Aid Despite Rescue-Team Dispute
detail: Mexico completed its third logistical flight of humanitarian aid to Colombia via Mexican Air Force aircraft, bringing the total to roughly 58 tonnes of drinking water, medicine, and rescue equipment for communities affected by the earthquake, even as diplomatic friction persisted over Colombia's earlier rejection of a Mexican rescue brigade. Colombian Foreign Minister Omar Bula confirmed acceptance of 58.5 tonnes of Mexican aid, and President Claudia Sheinbaum reaffirmed Mexico's solidarity with the Colombian people. Israel and Chile also delivered aid shipments during the week, and the IFRC launched a CHF 25 million appeal to scale up the Colombian Red Cross's response.

media.caption: Mexico's third aid flight lands in Colombia as the IFRC scales up its appeal

title: Leaked Letter Reveals Ousted UNGRD Chief Rejected International Rescue Teams
detail: A letter surfaced showing that Javier Pava, the outgoing UNGRD (disaster management) director appointed under President Petro, told Colombia's Foreign Ministry on August 11 that international search-and-rescue teams were 'not necessary at this stage of the emergency' given domestic capacity — a decision made as the earthquake's 72-hour survival window was closing. Pava left the UNGRD on August 12, when David Santiago Tamayo took over and reversed the policy, saying Colombia 'accepts and appreciates international aid wholeheartedly.' Colombian journalist Luis Carlos Vélez called the episode 'very serious,' asking whether officials were 'playing politics with people's lives'; by the time the letter became public, the confirmed death toll had reached 285, with 3,975 injured and 379 missing.

media.caption: Leaked letter shows former UNGRD chief Javier Pava rejected international rescue offers
